title: Andon reserved keys in a ledger issue
description: The keys Andon reserves in issues/<id>/issue.yaml, as readers take them from `kanban show <id> --json` (.issue). The ledger format allows and keeps any other key, so other keys are not checked here. The Chief of Staff writes these keys with `kanban set`, which stores every value as a string. A missing or unknown value is treated as missing by readers (the gate answers needs_human); keys with a default say so.

review.description: Whether an independent review is part of the issue. Missing: the gate answers needs_human and the dispatcher does not start a reviewer.

must_fix.description: Findings of this severity or heavier must be fixed by the issue's agent. Missing: the gate answers needs_human.

reviewer.description: Reviewer profile. Default: the other brand than the implementing profile (Claude -> codex-review, Codex -> claude-review).

review_rounds.description: Upper limit of review rounds, an integer of 1 or more written as a string (kanban set stores strings). Default: "2".

merge.description: auto: the dispatcher may merge after the gate approves, within the delegation. person: stop and notify the person. Default: person. It can only narrow the delegation.

machine.description: Machine name in the terminal host where the worker and reviewer run. Default: the same machine as the Chief of Staff.

deliverable.description: What the issue delivers. pr: a pull request (fix issues, Chief Engineer documents). candidates: library/candidates.json without a pull request (survey issues); andon issue submit asks for the file instead of a PR and the dispatcher does not run the gate. report: the report, and a pull request is optional (verification after apply, check issues added by routines, reviews after merge); a pull request it does open goes the same way as a pr issue, and the dispatcher does not tell an issue waiting on it that it was abandoned (ADR-0066). report counts only when the Chief of Staff at the time wrote it; otherwise it reads as pr. Default: pr.

estimate.description: The Chief of Staff's rough estimate of the issue's size, written when cutting the brief (ADR-0014). small: about 30 minutes, medium: about 60, large: about 120 of work without waits (a guide, not a limit). Only for worker issues (fix and survey), not reviewers or the Chief Engineer. No default: missing means no estimate, and nothing is compared.

acceptance.description: Numbers of the acceptance criteria the issue must meet, comma-separated without spaces and spelled as the report's acceptance[].id (A4,A13). The Chief of Staff writes it when cutting the issue (ADR-0035). andon issue submit refuses while the report has no acceptance[] row for one of them, and refuses a malformed value. Missing: the issue names no criteria and nothing is checked.

hold.description: The Chief of Staff holds the issue's pull request until the answer of this issue (its id) is reflected (ADR-0056). Written by andon issue hold and removed by andon issue unhold. While it holds, the gate does not run (andon issue gate answers wait), the dispatcher does not merge and discards a gate decision made before the hold, the gate's commit status is yellow, and andon waiting list keeps the pull request out of the merge requests. An empty value whose last change in log.jsonl was written by the issue's own worker terminal (or its reviewer's) still holds. The reason issue being done does not release it. Missing: not held.

later.description: The Chief of Staff leaves the issue's owner waits (decisions and tasks) for later: why it does not hurry, one line (ADR-0062). Trusted only when the row in log.jsonl that last changed it was written by the Chief of Staff terminal of that time and has the current value. andon waiting list reads it only on an owner issue or a todo or queued issue, and still calls when later_until has come or an issue behind it cannot wait. Missing: the waits call the owner.

later_until.description: The day (YYYY-MM-DD, in the ledger's timezone) from which an issue with later calls the owner again. Read as come when it is malformed or was not last written by the Chief of Staff terminal of that time. Missing: no day.

stacked_on.description: The earlier issue (its id, one of after) whose pull request branch this issue was started on (ADR-0067). Written by the Chief of Staff terminal when the issue is started on top, removed by the worker's restack. Trusted only together with stacked_base, when the rows in log.jsonl that last changed both keys were written by the Chief of Staff terminal of that time and have the current values; an untrusted key reads as missing. While trusted, kanban does not count the earlier issue as waited on. Missing: not stacked.

stacked_base.description: The commit the stacked issue's branch was cut from (the earlier issue's pull request head at that time; ADR-0067). While stacked, the gate, the review check and the reviewer's brief count the issue's diff from this commit to the head, not from the pull request's base. Trusted the same way as stacked_on. Missing: not stacked.

review_base.description: On a reviewer's issue: the commit the reviewed diff was counted from (the stacked_base of the reviewed issue; ADR-0067). The review check counts the reviewed commit's diff from it, so the review carries over a clean restack. Written by the dispatcher (terminal:dispatcher) and trusted only when the dispatcher terminal wrote the last change and the value is the current one. Missing: counted from the merge base with the default branch.
